name: Cable Lateral Raise
description: The cable lateral raise is a unilateral shoulder isolation exercise using a low cable pulley. Unlike the dumbbell version, the cable maintains constant tension throughout the full range of motion, including at the bottom where gravity removes load on a dumbbell. This makes it particularly effective for sustained lateral deltoid stimulation.

execution.starting_position: Stand beside a low cable pulley with the cable attachment in the hand farthest from the machine. The cable passes in front of your body. Hold a natural stance with the arm hanging at the side.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the pulley to the lowest position. Attach a single handle. Stand far enough from the stack to feel tension at the bottom of the movement.
steps: With a slight elbow bend, raise the arm out to the side away from the cable machine.
Raise until the upper arm is parallel to the floor.
Lower under control, maintaining tension on the cable throughout.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the raise, inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Standing too close to the machine, losing the constant tension benefit
Raising the arm too high above parallel
safety_considerations: Keep the working shoulder's path controlled — avoid shrugging the trap to lift the arm
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full bottom position with arm at side, raise to parallel at top.
coaching_cues: Lead with the elbow, not the wrist
Squeeze the lateral delt at the top of each rep
